results.title: In Ghana, political principles fly economy until their owners enter government!
results.content: Once upon a time in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, there lived two political parties that agreed on almost everything except who should enjoy the privileges they so passionately condemned. Whenever one party occupied the presidential palace, a presidential aircraft became an essential instrument of national security, diplomatic engagement and efficient governance. But the moment that party crossed into opposition, the same aircraft suddenly became an extravagant symbol of misplaced priorities, complete with luxurious seats, expensive fuel and a first-class ticket to political hypocrisy.

results.title: Tourism Ministry says Christmas events can boost Ghana’s December visitor appeal
results.content: The Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts says Christmas activities organised by churches and other institutions can strengthen Ghana’s appeal as a destination for visitors during the festive season. Deputy Director for Finance and Administration at the Ministry, Charles Sedem Hottor, said such initiatives complement government’s preparations for the influx of visitors expected in December. He made the remarks at the Christmas celebration organised by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints under the theme, “The Miracle of Christmas”.

results.title: One presidential jet, dishonest politicians, rented press and gullible citizens
results.content: Imagine this: in today’s commercial aviation, airlines are required to submit advance passenger information to authorities at the destination airport. If the President of Ghana were to be flying on a commercial airline, the commercial airline that the President of Ghana is flying on to the United States, for example, would submit this information to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). What if this information gets into the hands of a terrorist organisation? Your guess is as good as mine, if your brains can help you to imagine the consequences.

results.title: COP 31: Africa expresses profound disappointment with outcomes, questions Presidency’s handling of negotiations
results.content: The African Group of Negotiators (AGN) has expressed profound disappointment with the outcomes of key negotiations at the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, raising concerns over the substance of decisions and the process leading to their adoption. Speaking at the closing plenary, Chair of the African Group of Negotiators, Nana Dr. Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, said the outcomes on Action for Climate Empowerment (ACE) and long-term climate finance failed to adequately reflect Africa’s concerns and negotiating positions. COP31 closing plenary travelled to midnight on Saturday as negotiators remained deadlocked over whether the final agreement should explicitly address the phase-out of fossil fuels and provide support for vulnerable countries to adapt to climate change.

results.title: Kisseman–Christian Village bridge to close for six months for reconstruction
results.content: he bridge linking Kisseman and Christian Village in Accra will be closed to traffic for six months from the second week of December to allow for its reconstruction and elevation under the Greater Accra Resilient and Integrated Development (GARID) Project. The works are intended to improve the flow of rainwater through the area and reduce the risk of flooding during periods of heavy rainfall. GARID Project Communication Specialist, Philip Dunyo, said that alternative routes had been arranged to minimise the disruption to motorists who regularly use the busy road. He said drivers travelling from Achimota would be directed onto a route near a mosque before reaching the bridge, while those coming from Dome would use an alternative route at BJ Junction. “The road is a very busy road, and as a result, we have made alternative routes for motorists to use. results.title: Prof Nunoo calls for automated fisheries management to curb political interference
results.content: Professor of Fisheries Science at the University of Ghana, Francis Kofi Ewusie Nunoo, has called for greater automation in Ghana’s fisheries sector, arguing that the use of modern technology could strengthen enforcement and reduce political interference in management decisions. He said the sector’s reliance on human decisions had weakened the enforcement of regulations and made it difficult for scientists and regulators to implement measures based on research evidence. Prof Nunoo believes technologies such as drones, satellites and artificial intelligence (AI) could improve monitoring, surveillance and enforcement, while reducing the scope for undue human influence. He made the remarks at the launch of his memoir, Tides and Waves of Grace: A Memoir, in Accra. results.title: 22-year-old Ghanaian man dies after apartment fire in New York
results.content: A 22-year-old Ghanaian man, identified as Zaidan Harun, has died after an apartment fire in the Soundview neighbourhood of the Bronx, New York. The fire broke out shortly after 12:20 p.m. on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at a residential building on Metcalf Avenue, according to reports by 12 Westchester. Fire officials said the blaze started on the second floor before spreading to the floor above. Harun, who lived in an apartment on the second floor, was rescued by firefighters and taken to Jacobi Medical Center, where he later died.

results.title: Jospong subsidiary partners Turkish firm to test shrimp-shell-based farm products in Ghana
results.content: The African Agribusiness Consortium Limited (AAC), a subsidiary of the Jospong Group of Companies, has signed a memorandum of understanding with Türkiye-based ChitoGlobal Biotechnology to test agricultural products derived from discarded shrimp and crab shells on farms in Ghana. The agreement, signed on the sidelines of COP31 in Antalya, will begin with joint research and field trials to assess the products' suitability for Ghanaian farming conditions. The products are based on chitosan, a substance derived from chitin, which is naturally found in the shells of crustaceans. The trials will examine whether the products can protect seeds and plants, improve crop resilience during dry spells and strengthen plants' natural defences against fungal diseases.

results.title: Haruna Iddrisu announces €325m loan plan to address water shortages in three Northern cities
results.content: Education Minister and Tamale South MP, Haruna Iddrisu, says a €325 million loan agreement to support water infrastructure projects in Tamale, Damongo and Yendi will be laid before Parliament next week. He made the announcement at a ceremony in Tamale organised by members of Ahlussunna wal Jama'a (ASWAJ) to celebrate the selection of Sheikh Ibrahim Basha Iddris, popularly known as Sheikh Bayaan, as the group's interim National Imam. Addressing the gathering, Mr Iddrisu said Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson would present the agreement to Parliament. “Next week, the Finance Minister, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, will lay before Parliament a loan agreement of 325 million euros to end the water crisis in Tamale, Damongo, and Yendi,” he said.

results.title: All 16 regional best farmers to receive pick-up vehicles at 2026 Farmers’ Day
results.content: All 16 regional best farmers will receive brand-new pick-up vehicles at this year’s National Farmers’ Day celebration, the Minister of Food and Agriculture, Eric Opoku, has announced. The national best farmer with a disability will also receive a pick-up vehicle and GH¢200,000 at the 42nd edition of the celebration, scheduled for Friday, December 4, 2026, at the University of Energy and Natural Resources (UENR) in Sunyani. Mr Opoku announced the awards during a courtesy call on the Paramount Chief of the Sunyani Traditional Area, Odeefour Ogyeamansan Boahen Korkor II, at the Nana Bosoma Royal Palace in Asufufu, a suburb of Sunyani. The visit was to formally invite the traditional ruler to chair the opening session of the national celebration. results.title: Vanderpuye vows to rebuild and unite NDC if elected National Chairman
results.content: National Democratic Congress (NDC) National Chairmanship aspirant Edwin Nii Lante Vanderpuye has pledged to rebuild and unite the party, promising to overhaul its structures and restore its founding values if elected. Speaking at his campaign launch in Kumasi on Saturday, November 21, 2026, Mr Vanderpuye said his ambition was to rebuild the NDC and strengthen it for future electoral contests. “I want to rebuild the NDC so that the moral spirit with which we started the party shall be lifted once again. The NPP have not seen enough yet. They are going to see a political mechanic who will overhaul the NDC vehicle in this region and take it to that battle and win,” he stated. Mr Vanderpuye said the party needed to reconnect with its founding values, particularly solidarity and mutual support among members.

results.title: Vanderpuye vows to end NPP dominance in Ashanti Region if elected NDC Chairman
results.content: National Democratic Congress (NDC) National Chairmanship aspirant Edwin Nii Lante Vanderpuye has vowed to end the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) dominance in the Ashanti Region, saying he intends to make the region a major electoral base for the NDC. Speaking at his campaign launch in Kumasi on Saturday, November 21, 2026, Mr Vanderpuye said the region was crucial to the party’s prospects in future elections. “Without the Ashanti Region, the NDC will not be NDC,” he stated. He said his election as National Chairman would send a message to the NPP that its traditional electoral stronghold could become a competitive battleground.

results.title: “Even if it keeps you out of power, support $10bn programme” – Mahama to Minority
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama has urged the Minority in Parliament to support the government’s $10 billion New Economy programme, saying its success would benefit Ghana even if it prolongs the governing National Democratic Congress’ (NDC) stay in power. Speaking at the Head of State National Golf Tournament on Saturday, November 21, 2026, the President described the initiative as a national development agenda rather than a partisan project. He called on political leaders, financial institutions and private sector players to work together to achieve its objectives. President Mahama said the programme would involve investing $10 billion over four years in sectors with the potential to create jobs. He said the private sector and financial institutions would drive much of the investment, with the government providing guarantees to enable lenders to finance businesses and projects.

results.title: Nii Lante Vanderpuye promises pension scheme for NDC workers if elected National Chairman
results.content: National Democratic Congress (NDC) National Chairmanship aspirant Edwin Nii Lante Vanderpuye has pledged to introduce a pension scheme for party workers at all levels if elected to lead the party. He said the proposed scheme would cover workers from the branch level through to the constituency, regional and national levels, providing financial support for those who have dedicated years to party activities. Speaking during his campaign, Mr Vanderpuye said the fund would be financed through a proposed one per cent contribution from the salaries of government appointees. “In this country, I am going to institute a pension scheme for the workers of the party from the branch level to the constituency level to the regional level and to the national level,” he said.

results.title: Ghana Shippers Authority to tighten regulatory oversight of shipping industry in 2027
results.content: The Ghana Shippers’ Authority (GSA) says it will strengthen regulatory oversight and enforcement in 2027 to protect importers and exporters and address persistent challenges in the country’s shipping and logistics industry. Chief Executive Officer of the Authority, Professor Ransford Gyampo, said the focus would be on translating the expanded mandate under the Ghana Shippers’ Authority Act, 2024 (Act 1122), into measurable improvements for the shipping community. He outlined the priorities at a media engagement in Accra, where the Authority also acknowledged the media’s role in informing the public, promoting accountability and shaping national discourse. Prof Gyampo said the GSA would prioritise the regulation of shipping charges, enforcement of service standards and protection of shippers’ interests.

results.title: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
results.content: Negotiations at the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkey are in deadlock after running more than 36 hours into overtime with countries unable to agree on a new global climate deal.

results.title: Amputee World Cup: Repeat for Ghana or revenge for Morocco?
results.content: For Ghana, the opportunity is to crown an impressive campaign with a maiden world title, while Morocco will be seeking revenge for two painful defeats against their West African rivals.

results.title: Ghana-Morocco final brings African Paralympic chiefs together on opposite sides
results.content: Deen is travelling to San Juan De Lagos, Mexico on a private jet and will be joined at the final by the African Paralympic Committee’s Second Vice-President, Morocco’s Hamid El Aouni, as the two African nations battle for the world title.

results.title: Senior high schools still using firewood and charcoal in their kitchens urged to adopt LPG
results.content: Senior high schools still using firewood and charcoal in their kitchens have been urged to adopt Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) because of health consequences of prolonged exposure to inhalation of smoke from charcoal and firewood.

results.title: Mamdani announces plan to close New York’s Rikers Island jail by 2032
results.content: New York City's official overseeing the closure of the city's most notorious jail hopes a new plan from Mayor Zohran Mamdani will lead to "a moment of transformation" for how people are detained in the largest US city.

results.title: Man killed in suspected scrambler hit-and-run
results.content: A man has been killed following a collision with a vehicle believed to be a scrambler motorcycle, gardaí (Irish police) have said.

results.title: Universities must rethink media education as media industry shifts towards entrepreneurship – Prof Sikanku
results.content: Associate Professor of Journalism and Political Communication and Dean of the School of Journalism and Media Studies (SOJAMS) at the University of Media, Arts and Communication (UniMAC), Professor Godwin Etse Sikanku, has called on universities to rethink media education to prepare students for the changing economics of the media industry.

results.title: ‘Leadership is not personal property’ – ASWAJ reaffirms NADAC’s sole authority to elect National Imam
results.content: The National Da’wa Council (NADAC) of the Ahlussunna Wal Jama’a (ASWAJ) has reaffirmed its constitutional mandate to elect the National Imam and his deputies, declaring that "leadership is not personal property" and that the authority to elect leadership does not rest with any individual, family, or external group.

results.title: Man’s penis reattached at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital after accident
results.content: Surgeons at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital have successfully reattached a man’s severed penis in a rare and complex procedure, the hospital’s Board Chair, Professor Titus Beyuo, has disclosed.

results.title: ‘Give us back our school’ – Mfantsipim Old Boys appeal to government
results.content: The Mfantsipim Old Boys Association (MOBA) has called on the government to reconsider the management structure of Mfantsipim School and allow the association to assume greater responsibility for its development through a restructured partnership with the state and the Methodist Church.

results.title: Techiman North inaugurates 58 sanitation guards to boost cleanliness and create jobs
results.content: The Techiman North District Assembly has inaugurated 58 sanitation guards tasked with keeping the district clean and healthy, in a move to tackle poor sanitation and youth unemployment simultaneously.

results.title: Asiedu Nketiah urges Africa to turn reparations declarations into practical action
results.content: National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, has called on African governments and political leaders to move beyond declarations on reparative justice and pursue practical measures capable of securing redress for historical injustices. He says Africa has made significant progress in building the institutional framework for reparations but must now give the process greater political support and ensure that commitments translate into enforceable remedies. Addressing the Movement for Freedom of Nations Assembly in Moscow on November 16, 2026, Mr Asiedu Nketiah said the African Union had established mechanisms to develop a common position on reparations and was working with Caribbean institutions to coordinate legal analysis and diplomacy.

results.title: Ashantis deserve more than loans of their stolen royal regalia – Asiedu Nketiah
results.content: The National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, says the Asante people deserve more than temporary access to their royal heritage, insisting that the return of looted regalia on loan from British museums cannot be equated with full restitution. He says the distinction between a loan and a transfer of ownership is important in assessing whether communities whose cultural treasures were taken during colonial conquest have received meaningful redress.

results.title: Bono East Regional Minister reaffirms gov’t commitment to infrastructure and job creation at Offuman Fofie Yam Festival
results.content: The Bono East Regional Minister, Francis Owusu Antwi, joined the Paramount Chief of the Offuman Traditional Area, Nana Kwaku Gyan Borokuo II, for the grand durbar of the Offuman Traditional Council’s 2026 Annual Fofie Yam Festival, where he reaffirmed the government's commitment to improving infrastructure and creating jobs.

results.title: Man remanded for allegedly stealing girlfriend’s GH¢18,500
results.content: A 32-year-old man has been remanded into police custody by the Madina District Court for allegedly stealing GH¢18,500 belonging to his girlfriend after she refused to loan him money to start a business.
